title: Test churn keeps fseventsd at a full core and 7 GB
what: Measure how much of the gate's system time comes from file events (one gate with TMPDIR on the main volume and one with TMPDIR on a separate APFS volume or RAM disk whose .fseventsd/no_log stops event logging), and if it pays, make relay gate and the tests put their temporary folders there by default, created by relay setup, with a fallback when it is missing.
why: 29 Oct ~15:40, front, top: with 6 lanes gating, fseventsd uses 105% CPU and 6.9 GB of memory, kernel_task 23%, XprotectService and syspolicyd 5-6% each; CPU 76% system, 23% user, load 36 on 12 cores, after the podman machine was cut to 8 GiB and swap fell from 6.4 to 1.6 GB. The tests create and delete thousands of temporary git repositories on the main volume, and macOS logs every file event and scans new files. The system time, not the tests, takes most of the CPU, so gates run several times slower than their own work.
failing_case: top during 6 gating lanes shows fseventsd at about 100% CPU and CPU usage about 75% system.
pass_cases: with the gate's temporary folders on the no-log volume, fseventsd stays under 10% CPU during a gate
the gate's wall time and system time are measured before and after and written in the report
a machine without the volume still gates, with one line naming relay setup

fact: 30 Oct, measured by the build (load 17-25): tests/test_gate.py (36 tests) on the main volume 105.4 s wall, fseventsd 128-140% CPU and 5.8-7.0 GB; the same on a 2 GB APFS RAM disk with .fseventsd/no_log holding the tests' temporary folders 105.6 s, fseventsd 116-162% CPU and 6.7-7.1 GB. fseventsd was at about 130% before the run started: the load is machine-wide (other gate lanes, podman, git worktrees), not the tests' temporary folders. Nothing was changed.

question: **macOS file-watch service at a full core: drop the item or move every worktree to a no-log disk?**

macOS's file-change service (fseventsd) uses 1.3-1.6 cores and about 7 GB. The build measured that moving the tests' temporary folders to a RAM disk with change logging off changes nothing: the load comes from the whole machine (six lanes of worktrees, podman, git), not from the tests. The only untried step is putting every lane's worktree on such a disk. You are moving development to Linux VMs, where this service does not exist.
options: a. Drop the item: it ends with the move to Linux; nothing changes on the Mac
b. Try moving every lane's worktree to a no-log disk on the Mac (about 60 agent minutes, changes where relay puts worktrees)
answer: Хорошо сними пункт, когда ты отвечаешь на вопрос самостоятельно - делаешь ли ты пометку об этом в задаче, есть ли там пометка о том что выбор сделал именно ты ?
reading: a: drop the item; it ends with the move to Linux.
